chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: When the believer dies, satans numbering as many as Rabi‘ah and Mudar are let loose upon his neighbors, who had been preoccupied with him.

key_terms.الشَّيَاطِينِ: the satans; evil beings that bring misguidance and harm
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer; a person of faith whose presence brings spiritual benefit
key_terms.جِيرَانِهِ: his neighbors; the people living around him
key_terms.عَدَدَ رَبِيعَةَ وَمُضَرَ: as numerous as the tribes of Rabi‘ah and Mudar; an expression of great multitude
key_terms.مُشْتَغِلِينَ بِهِ: preoccupied with him; occupied or engaged because of him

ai.seo_question: What happens to a believer’s neighbors when the believer dies according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a hidden consequence that follows the death of a believer, indicating that his presence had been a form of protection for those around him. It underscores the spiritual benefit of the believer within society and points to the unseen harms that may emerge when such a person departs.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘
When the Momin dies, the Satansla of the number of the (tribes of) Rabi’e and Muzar are freed to be upon his neighbours, who used to be pre-occupied with him’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ‘ Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir who has said the following: “I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘
When a believer dies the devils working to mislead him, now released among his neighbors, number equal to all the people of the tribe of Rabi’ and Mudar.’”
